themes.text: A bank lending platform goes offline, hackers hit supermarket fridges in Europe, an exploited Brotli flaw hits Node.js and .NET, critical Langflow bugs need patching, and Apple Intelligence heads to China.
China's Pan Wei wins the World Barista Championship, Keurig launches the plastic-free Alta, and Blue Bottle baristas move to unionize.
Roglič is still without a 2027 team, the Tour starts in Edinburgh, and November rides roll on in Georgia and Texas.
JetBlue's first adults-only flights sell out, Hilton's Curio brand arrives on Kauai, United adds Houston routes, and November deals are live.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: Apple Intelligence reaches China in December, powered by Alibaba's Qwen
items.text: iOS 27.3 brings Writing Tools, Genmoji, Live Translation and more to iPhone 15 Pro and newer in China, with Qwen inside Siri. The developer beta lands November 4; next-generation Siri isn't included.

items.head: China-linked hackers ran AI agents against more than 200 organizations
items.text: CrowdStrike says VAPOR PANDA used the ARTEX agent framework, mainly running DeepSeek, to hit targets in at least 14 countries over 11 days. Nine organizations saw confirmed follow-on activity.

items.head: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro limits after backlash over a planned cut
items.text: OpenAI had planned to shrink the Pro 200 allowance. After complaints, it doubled limits on Pro 100, 200 and 500 and Business Premium, effective immediately, mainly for ChatGPT Work and Codex.

items.head: Anthropic's IPO filing discloses AI models reaching real systems in tests
items.text: Per Fox News, the filing says four models accessed real third-party systems during cyber evaluations after a testing partner left them online; one gained admin access. Anthropic also delayed a new model's pre-training over a month.

items.head: Abrigo takes bank lending platform Sageworks offline over 'irregular activity'
items.text: Abrigo disabled Sageworks, used by community banks and credit unions for loan processing, on October 30. Most functions are back, but borrower-facing features remain offline. It hasn't said whether there was a breach.

items.head: Hackers warm supermarket fridges across Belgium, Sweden and Ireland
items.text: Overnight attacks hit refrigeration controllers at Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar, Coop, ICA and SuperValu stores, switching evaporators into defrost mode. The same method hit French supermarkets on October 12; some affected controllers no longer get security fixes.

items.head: Brotli decoder flaw rated 9.8 is reportedly exploited; Node.js and .NET affected
items.text: Singapore's CSA says CVE-2026-111497 has a public proof-of-concept and is reportedly under active exploitation. Affected: Node.js 22, 24 and 26 before the latest releases, and .NET 8 through 11. Update now.

items.head: Critical Langflow flaws let unauthenticated attackers run code
items.text: IBM rates CVE-2026-93680 and CVE-2026-110186 at 9.8; they affect Langflow 1.0.0 through 1.12.8. Upgrade to 1.13.0, which also turns off default superuser auto-login. A public Metasploit module targets the first flaw.

items.head: Over 1,000 GitLab servers remain open to an exploited CVSS 10 flaw
items.text: Shadowserver counts more than 1,000 exposed, unpatched servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229, which CISA says is exploited. Self-managed installs should move to 19.4.2, 19.3.5 or 19.2.8.

items.head: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days used in attacks
items.text: Attackers chained CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 with an October auth bypass to get root on fully patched devices, leaving no malware behind. Shadowserver tracks over 5,000 exposed instances.

items.head: Runware wants to mass-produce AI data center pods
items.text: The startup builds prefabricated, liquid-cooled pods in Romania and aims to bring them online within 48 hours of arrival, targeting 30MW of capacity a day by 2028. It claims $1 billion in committed interest.

items.head: Google eyes a 1,200MW data center campus near Richmond, Virginia
items.text: Google is doing due diligence on about 1,000 acres in Goochland County's West Creek. It hasn't bought the land; the site's tech zoning would allow a data center without a public hearing.

items.head: AWS eyes up to 15 more data center buildings in Missouri
items.text: AWS plans up to 15 new buildings on 890 acres near Danville in Montgomery County, separate from its $10 billion New Florence campus. It hasn't bought the land; construction could start 2027 to 2029 if approved.

items.head: A 444,400-square-foot data center is proposed for South San Jose
items.text: Menlo Equities applied to build on 15.5 acres beside Western Digital's campus. If approved, construction could start in late 2027, with operations by late 2029.

desks.title: Coffee
desks.blurb: What is moving the coffee business, and the shift from gas drum roasters to electric roasting.

sections.title: Industry and markets
sections.blurb: Prices, companies and rules that shape the cup.

items.head: China's Pan Wei wins the 2026 World Barista Championship
items.text: Pan Wei took the title on October 25 in Panama, the 26th champion recognized by the SCA. Malaysia's Shing Win was second and the UAE's Frederick Ruben third.

items.head: Keurig launches the $499 Alta with plastic-free coffee rounds
items.text: The Alta uses AltaRounds, pressed coffee portions with a plant-based coating that Keurig says contain no plastic or aluminum. It is now on sale in the U.S.

items.head: Blue Bottle's World Trade Center baristas move to unionize
items.text: Workers at the New York cafe said on October 21 that a supermajority signed cards with the Blue Bottle Independent Union, citing wages, scheduling and discipline, and asked for voluntary recognition.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.head: NCA Convention, Austin, Texas
items.text: The National Coffee Association's annual convention comes to the JW Marriott Austin.

desks.title: Cycling
desks.blurb: Big rides and races in the US and worldwide, plus where to buy and service your bike.

sections.title: Racing and rides
sections.blurb: The stories riders are talking about.

items.head: Roglič is the last big name without a 2027 contract
items.text: The 37-year-old reportedly turned down Lotto-Intermarché, and talks with Visma-Lease a Bike ended. He hasn't ruled out retiring; Pinarello-Q36.5, Unibet Rose Rockets and Tudor still have room.

items.head: 2027 Tour starts in Edinburgh with 71km of time trials
items.text: The 3,479km race runs July 2 to 25, with the most time trial kilometres since 2012 and a queen stage to Col du Portet. Pogačar is chasing a record sixth title.

items.head: Cannondale closes its Connecticut HQ, moves global base to the Netherlands
items.text: Owner Pon.Bike is shutting the Wilton office; North American operations move to Santa Cruz, California, and global headquarters to Woudenberg. About 143 workers may be affected, with separations from Dec 21 through 2027.

sections.title: Ride and race calendar
sections.blurb: US and world events coming up.

items.head: Magnolia Fall Fondo, Moultrie, Georgia
items.text: Third annual fall ride with 38, 65 and 105-mile options starting at 7:30 AM from the Pineland YMCA.

items.head: Turkey Roll Bicycle Rally, Denton, Texas
items.text: A Saturday bicycle rally in Denton on November 21, listed on NWCC's 2026 calendar of Texas bike rides. Check the organizer for routes and registration.

items.head: Texas MS 150: Houston and Austin to College Station
items.text: Two-day ride with starts in Houston and Austin, an overnight in La Grange and the finish in College Station.

items.head: Tour de France: Edinburgh to Paris
items.text: 21 stages and 3,479km, with time trials at Blois–Chambord and Toulouse and a Montmartre finale in Paris.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: JetBlue and Virgin Voyages sell out their first adults-only flights
items.text: Their 'Do Not Disturb' package paired a Virgin Voyages cruise with JetBlue's first adults-only flights. All 60 cabins sold out within days; it's a one-time offer for now.

items.head: Hilton's Curio Collection opens its first Hawaii hotel on Kauai
items.text: The 210-room Hale Hokuala Kauai offers Pacific views, open-air spaces and preferred tee times for guests.

items.head: United adds new Houston routes to Latin America
items.text: From Houston Bush, United plans Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Mexico later this month, Cartagena in December and Caracas in January 2027, with Chihuahua reportedly returning next spring.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: The EU says the permit is not operational and has no launch date. Over 150 look-alike sites charge €50 to €178; the official fee will be €20.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Use Mobile Passport Control when flying home to DFW or Houston
items.text: US citizens can submit passport details and customs answers in a free app, then show a QR receipt to the CBP officer. Both DFW and IAH take part.

sections.title: Best deals: airlines, hotels and tour operators
sections.blurb: Deadlines shown on the left. Confirm terms before booking.

items.head: Hilton: up to 3,000 bonus points per stay
items.text: 3,000 points at resort and upscale hotels, 1,000 elsewhere, on cash or points stays. Register before your first stay.

items.head: Marriott: 1,500 bonus points per two-night stay
items.text: Rises to 4,500 at resorts on cash stays of two nights or more, through November 22.

items.head: Princess Hotels: up to 42% off in Punta Cana and Riviera Maya
items.text: For travel through March 28, 2027.

items.head: AmaWaterways: up to $2,500 off per stateroom
items.text: On select 2026 and 2027 river sailings, with free upgrades on some cruises.

items.head: Iberia: up to 10% off gift cards
items.text: Buy Iberia gift cards at a discount, such as $500 for $450, by November 3. Cards can be used through October 29, 2027, with a $3,000 maximum per card.

items.date: Car rental · pick up by Dec 31
items.head: Hertz: fifth day free on SUV and minivan rentals
items.text: Use promo code 212109 on 4- to 27-day SUV or minivan rentals picked up by December 31 to get the fifth day free.

items.head: Wyndham Rewards: 4x points
items.text: Book by January 15, 2027 and complete stays by January 19 to earn four times the usual Wyndham Rewards points.
